Gunna.brief: Atlanta melodic trap with a short pocket. In this catalog the median bar is 11 syllables, about half the lines sit at 10-14, and the 15-19 stretch is the minority. Designer flex and a quieter pain line share the verse. Keep Wunna, drip, YSL, Patek, VVS, Dior, biscotti, and slatt when they fit. Henny is uncommon, so use it sparingly. End words lean on it, yeah, and me. Pairs that repeat are ride/slide, choice/voice, and check/neck. Songs that mark the voice here are WUNNA, fukumean, pushin P, one of wun, and Drip Too Hard.

Lil Baby.brief: Atlanta street rap with a longer bar. The median is 12 syllables, a quarter of the lines run 15-19, and the upper band reaches about 17. The verse stays on the trenches, the plug, the bros, and a plain claim of being real, with romance when that topic is tagged. House words are brodie, 4PF, dawg, racks, hundred, trenches, and plug. Woah is the ad-lib. End rhymes stay plain: day/way, good/hood, all/ball, and deal/real. Anthems in this index are Woah, Yes Indeed, Drip Too Hard, The Bigger Picture, Close Friends, and My Dawg.

Drake.brief: Toronto talk-rap. The median bar is 11 syllables, with a wide middle from 8 to 14. Romance is the biggest tagged topic. The line sounds like someone moving through the night, and the end words pile up on me, you, yeah, time, and know. House tags are Drizzy, OVO, 6ix, Toronto, and Issa. Guest names in a collab row stay guests. Pairs that repeat are face/place, alone/phone, and feel/real. Anthems in this index are Rich Flex, First Person Shooter, Passionfruit, Jimmy Cooks, Laugh Now Cry Later, and Nonstop. Long battle-rap transcripts under this artist string are not the voice.

Lil Wayne.brief: New Orleans punchline rap, and the largest set in this index. The median is 11 syllables, and a third of the bars are 9 or shorter, so the turn lands before the line grows. About one in five bars carries three or more inner rhymes, the most of any artist here in raw count. House tags are Weezy, Tunechi, Hollygrove, and Tha Carter. End pairs that repeat are dead/head, funny/money, good/hood, and game/name. Anthems are A Milli, Drop the World, She Will, Right Above It, Uproar, Mr. Carter, Go DJ, and Fireman. Stack one metaphor, then end the bar.

NoCap.brief: NoCap writes the longest bars of these six. The median is 13 syllables, a third of the lines sit at 15-19, and the average is just under 13. The catalog clusters on pain, jail, opps, demons, tears, hope, and codeine. Mr. Crawford is the album name that shows up in the rows. Mobile and Alabama are rare as words here, so the verse should not hang on the city. End rhymes are sparse: pain/rain, news/shoes, and good/hood. Anthems are Pain Show, Vaccine, Mistake, Very Special, Blind Nights, and Shackles to Diamonds. Finish the long sentence.

Young Thug.brief: Short melodic bars: 1,731 lines and 35 songs, mostly So Much Fun. The median is 10 syllables, and 43 percent of the bars are 9 or under. Yeah, woah, hey, and ooh already take many of the endings. Words that clear the noise are diamonds, racks, woo, mate, surf, and slime. Slatt is present and smaller. Thugger is rare here. The iconic titles are Bad Bad Bad and Surf. The end pairs that repeat are day/today and daughter/water. Keep the bar short and leave room for the ad-lib. This credit is Young Thug, separate from Young Stoner Life.
